content1.content: Flutter: Super-fast Persistence with Isar Database

content2.content: While ObjectBox is a fantastic high-performance database, another top-tier competitor in the Flutter ecosystem is Isar. Built from the ground up for Dart and Flutter, Isar is an extremely fast, open-source, and feature-rich NoSQL database that has gained immense popularity for local data storage.

content3.content: This article will guide you through setting up and using Isar to manage your app's local data.

content4.content: What is Isar and Why Use It?

content5.content: Isar is a fully asynchronous, ACID-compliant, and statically-typed database. You work directly with Dart objects, and Isar's powerful engine, written in Rust, handles the storage and querying with incredible speed.

content7.content:
Extremely Fast: Performance is a primary design goal, with benchmarks showing it competes at the top with other high-performance embedded databases.
Feature-Rich: Supports complex queries, multi-entry indexes, full-text search, and JSON support out of the box.
ACID Compliance: Guarantees that your database transactions are Atomic, Consistent, Isolated, and Durable, protecting your data integrity.
Compile-Time Safe & Statically Typed: Isar's code generator creates type-safe queries, so you can catch errors at compile time, not at runtime.
Built-in Relations: Supports one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships (called Links) between your data collections.
Excellent Tooling: Comes with the Isar Inspector, a live-debugging tool that allows you to view, query, and edit your data in real-time during development.
Asynchronous Core: Designed to be fully async, with support for multi-isolate usage to prevent blocking the UI thread.

content9.content: Setting Up Isar in Your Flutter Project

content10.content: Setting up Isar is straightforward and relies on code generation to provide its excellent type safety and performance.

content12.content: Add the required packages to your pubspec.yaml file:

content13.content:
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  isar: ^3.1.0+1 # Use the latest version
  isar_flutter_libs: ^3.1.0+1 # Contains the native binaries for Isar
  path_provider: ^2.0.0 # To find the correct directory for the database

dev_dependencies:
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  build_runner: ^2.4.0 # Use the latest version
  isar_generator: ^3.1.0+1 # Use the latest version

content14.content: Run flutter pub get in your terminal.

content16.content: In Isar, a data model is called a "Collection." You define it by annotating a Dart class with @collection.

content22.content: Run the build_runner command to generate the necessary note.g.dart file.

content24.content: You must re-run this command whenever you change your collection classes.

content26.content: It's best practice to create a singleton or a helper class to manage the Isar instance.

content28.content: You can then create an instance of this service in your main.dart and make it available to your app, for example, using a state management solution like Riverpod or Provider.

content30.content: CRUD operations in Isar are performed within transactions. writeTxn is used for operations that modify the database.

content31.content: Let's assume you have an IsarService instance available as isarService.

content33.content: The put() method handles both creating a new object and updating an existing one. If the object's id is new, it's inserted; otherwise, it's updated.

content36.content: You can read all objects or query for specific ones.

content39.content: Isar provides a powerful and type-safe query builder.

content42.content: To remove an object, use delete() inside a write transaction.

content45.content: One of Isar's most powerful features is the ability to watch for changes in a query and reactively update your UI. The .watch() method returns a Stream that emits the new list of results whenever the data changes.

content49.content: Isar offers an outstanding developer experience with its speed, type-safety, and rich feature set. It provides a modern and powerful alternative to other local databases in Flutter. With features like the Isar Inspector, reactive queries, and easy-to-use relationships, it equips you with all the tools needed to handle complex local data persistence with ease. For new Flutter projects requiring a robust local database, Isar is an excellent choice.
